svg.text: Monitoring and incident management: event-driven architecture in ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
Security groups: Internet to ALB only, ALB to EC2 only, EC2 and Lambda to RDS only
EC2 and RDS have no public IP address. Outbound traffic leaves through the NAT Gateway.
The administrator opens the dashboard, and monitored
applications send events with their token. Both enter
through the Internet Gateway to the Application Load
The load balancer forwards to the EC2 app server in a
private subnet. Only the load balancer can reach it.
The worker on EC2 checks monitored websites on a schedule.
Traffic leaves through the NAT Gateway.
The app stores users, services and check results in RDS
Every check result and application event is put on an SQS
FIFO queue. Messages that keep failing go to a dead-letter
SQS triggers the Lambda function, which applies the
Lambda opens and resolves incidents in RDS.
When an incident opens or resolves, SNS emails the
Logs are archived to S3 (daily, or on demand from
and secrets) and IAM roles (least privilege) support EC2
and Lambda. AWS Budgets watches the bill.
Services: EC2 · VPC · ALB · NAT Gateway · RDS · SQS · Lambda
SNS · S3 · CloudWatch · Parameter Store · IAM · AWS Budgets
